name: F5 iApp APL
comment:
APL — the presentation language of an F5 iApp template. Not Tcl: it has its own grammar of sections, typed fields, attributes and choice lists, with `[ … ]` bracket expressions that *are* Tcl. Every Tcl-family language used to be pointed at `tcl.tmLanguage.json`, which contains no APL rule at all, so an APL file was painted with Tcl rules until the server answered and replaced them wholesale (issue #903). The scopes below are the ones `package.json` already maps the server's `apl*` semantic-token types to, so the static paint and the semantic paint agree instead of contradicting each other.

Every keyword alternation carries an explicit trailing boundary. Without one, `yesno` matches inside the *user-defined type name* `yesno_choice` (`define choice yesno_choice`) and paints half of it as a field-type keyword — a real bug the first draft of this grammar had.

A field's type may be user-defined (`define choice lb_method` … then `lb_method lb_algorithm`). A static grammar cannot know those names, so such a field is left unscoped rather than guessed at; the semantic layer types it correctly.

directive.comment: A preprocessor directive. Matched before #comment so `#include` is not swallowed as one.

embedded-tcl.comment: A bracket expression is Tcl, and the server walks it as Tcl. Painting it as Tcl here keeps the two layers in step.

define.comment: `define <field-type> <name> { … }` introduces a reusable type — the *second* word is the type being reused, the *third* is the new name. Getting this backwards scopes `choice` as the definition's name.

optional.comment: `optional ( <field> == "value" ) { … }` guards a block on a field's value. The condition is APL's own tiny expression language, not Tcl.

patterns.comment: A (possibly dotted) reference to another field.
patterns.name: variable.other.field.apl

section.comment: `section NAME {`, and the `text` / `table` / `row` block keywords. `text` may carry a locale string instead of a name (`text "de-DE" { … }`).

validator.comment: The validators APL ships with, named inside `validator "…"`. The whole construct is matched as one unit, quotes included: TextMate resolves competing patterns by which one starts *earliest*, not by list order, so the opening quote would otherwise start #string and the name inside would be painted as ordinary string content. Only a name in this position is a validator — a bare `Number` in `display "Number"` is not.

field.comment: A field declaration is `<field-type> <name> …`. The trailing `(?=\s)` boundary is load-bearing: without it `yesno` matches inside the user-defined type name `yesno_choice`.

choice-mapping.comment: A choice list maps a display label to a stored value: `"Round Robin" => "round-robin",`.
choice-mapping.name: keyword.operator.mapping.apl

variable.comment: APL supports Tcl-style variable substitution — `$name`, `$ns::name`, `$arr(idx)`, `${braced}`. Taken from bitwisecook/vscode-iApp, which had it and this grammar's first draft did not.
variable.name: variable.other.apl
